title: button groups
rule: Present related actions as a small cluster of buttons, aligned horizontally or vertically; split into more groups if there are more than three or four actions.

citation.source: Designing Interfaces 3e ch. Doing Things — Button Groups (Tidwell, Brewer, Valencia)

pass_when: Related actions sit in one small horizontal or vertical cluster; more than three or four are split into further groups.
fail_when: Related actions are scattered, or more than three or four sit in one undifferentiated strip.
overview: A small aligned cluster of related action buttons, split when the set grows.
apply_when: Presenting a few related actions side by side or stacked.
not_when: A large command set needs an action panel or overflow menu.
agent_hint: Cluster related buttons; split past three or four into further groups.
description: Related actions read as one unit when they sit in a small horizontal or vertical cluster rather than scattering across the chrome. Keep each cluster to about three or four buttons; past that, split into further groups so the strip stays scannable. Apply this to peer actions that share a role; do not force a huge tool set into one undifferentiated strip when an action panel or menu is the better home.
